definition: A blueprint is a detailed plan that specifies exactly how something will be built or carried out.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word blueprint. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know blueprint should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: Volunteers followed the barn-raising blueprint so faithfully that the frame stood by dusk without a single wasted cut.
An outline is looser than a blueprint: it names the plan's big pieces in order and stops, while a blueprint dictates dimensions, materials, and how every part joins.
Specification goes further than blueprint — a blueprint governs one build, while a specification sets exact tolerances that every builder, in every factory, must reproduce.
A schematic is the technician's diagram — it maps how a circuit's parts connect, all symbols and lines. A blueprint covers the whole build, dimensions included, from foundation to roofline.
A roadmap sequences a plan's stages over time — what happens first, next, and last. A blueprint specifies the finished thing itself: not when the parts arrive, but exactly how they fit.

When Coach Odom's tiny school somehow produced three straight championship relay teams, rival coaches began asking for her blueprint — and she handed it over freely: a binder that mapped every practice to the minute, every drill to a stopwatch split, every taper to the calendar's final week.
Copy it all you like, she warned; the binder builds the season, but you still have to supply the runners.

Blueprint is the right word because the binder doesn't merely gesture at a philosophy — it specifies the whole construction, down to minutes and splits, exactly the way a builder's drawing fixes every joint before the first nail.
Note the word's honest limit, too, and Odom names it: a blueprint tells you precisely how to build the thing, never whether your materials can bear it.
Blueprint keeps its hard hat even in figurative use: call a policy a blueprint and you are promising specifics — parts, order, measurements.
If the plan only names stages and dates, roadmap is the honest word; if it only sketches intentions, don't dress it in drafting paper.
This unit's methodical worker is exactly who a blueprint is written for.

When the city library digitized its archives, the star attraction was a roll of drawings for the 1911 carousel in Riverside Park.
The carousel itself burned in 1968, and for half a century it existed only in photographs.
The drawings turned out to be a complete blueprint, down to the curve of each horse's neck and the gauge of every bolt.
A restoration guild raised funds to rebuild, promising to follow the sheet exactly.
Three years later, riders could mount horses their great-grandparents would have recognized, carved to the same measurements recorded a century before.
